title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: SpatialData.plot package contains set plotting functions spatial omics data stored SpatialData .zarr files follow OME-NGFF specs. SpatialData object composed five layers: images, labels, shapes, points, tables. layer may contain arbitrary number elements. Images labels represented ZarrArrays (Rarr). Points shapes represented arrow objects linked -disk .parquet file. , data represented memory. Element annotation well cross-layer summarizations (e.g., count matrices) represented SingleCellExperiment tables. demonstrate package functionality using trivial example dataset. realistic technology-focused examples, refer readers companion demo website.
code: x <- file.path("extdata", "blobs.zarr") x <- system.file(x, package="spatialdataR") (x <- readSpatialData(x)) ## class: SpatialData ## - images(2): ##   - blobs_image (3,64,64) ##   - blobs_multiscale_image (3,64,64) ## - labels(2): ##   - blobs_labels (64,64) ##   - blobs_multiscale_labels (64,64) ## - points(1): ##   - blobs_points (200) ## - shapes(3): ##   - blobs_circles (5,circle) ##   - blobs_multipolygons (2,polygon) ##   - blobs_polygons (5,polygon) ## - tables(1): ##   - table (3,10) [blobs_labels] ## coordinate systems(5): ## - global(8): blobs_image blobs_multiscale_image ... blobs_polygons ##   blobs_points ## - scale(1): blobs_labels ## - translation(1): blobs_labels ## - affine(1): blobs_labels ## - sequence(1): blobs_labels

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: SpatialData.plot provides 5 user-facing plotting functions: plotSpatialData() renders base (blank) ggplot simple aesthetics , importantly, fixed axial ratio distort spatial coordinates. plotImage/Label/Point/Shape() render specific SpatialData elements; requires specification element index/name , coordinate system j (default, first available element/system rendered); different functions accept different arguments control aesthetics.

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: Image/LabelArrays linked potentially multiscale .zarr stores. show method includes scales available given element: Internally, multiscale ImageArrays stored list ZarrArray, e.g.: retrieve specific scale’s ZarrArray, can use data(., k), k specifies target scale. also works plotting:
code: image(x, "blobs_image") ## class:  SpatialDataImage   ## Scales (1): (3,64,64) image(x, "blobs_multiscale_image") ## class:  SpatialDataImage (MultiScale)  ## Scales (3): (3,64,64 3,32,32 3,16,16) i <- image(x, "blobs_multiscale_image") vapply(data(i, k=NULL), dim, numeric(3)) ##      [,1] [,2] [,3] ## [1,]    3    3    3 ## [2,]   64   32   16 ## [3,]   64   32   16 wrap_plots(nrow=1, lapply(seq(3), \(.)      plotSpatialData(x) + plotImage(i=2, k=.)))

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: Like images, labels represented ZarrArray. Array values, however, integers correspond different instances, typically linked table annotations (e.g., expression values, observation metadata, etc.).
code: i <- "blobs_labels" t <- getTable(x, i) t$id <- sample(letters, ncol(t)) table(x) <- t  p <- plotSpatialData(x) pal_d <- hcl.colors(10, "Spectral") pal_c <- hcl.colors(9, "Inferno")[-9]  a <- p + plotLabel(i = i, pal="grey")                   # binary b <- p + plotLabel(i = i, c="id", pal=pal_d)            # metadata c <- p + plotLabel(i = i, c="channel_1_sum", pal=pal_c) # assay  (a | b | c) +      plot_layout(guides="collect") &      theme(legend.position="bottom")

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: Elements points layer rendered using geom_point(), accepts discrete continuous color specifications.
code: i <- "blobs_points" a <- p + plotPoint(i = i) b <- p + plotPoint(i = i, col="genes")       # discrete c <- p + plotPoint(i = i, col="instance_id") # continuous (a | b | c)

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: demonstration, render shape element present object, includes possible types: circles (multi)polygons.
code: p <- plotSpatialData(x) a <- p +     labs(title = "polygons") +     plotShape(i = "blobs_polygons") b <- p +     labs(title = "multipolygons") +     plotShape(i = "blobs_multipolygons") c <- p +     labs(title = "circles") +     plotShape(i = "blobs_circles") (a | b | c)

title: `SpatialData.plot`
text: Several SpatialData elements (images, labels, points, shapes) can layered -top ggplot-style using +-operator. return value call remains ggplot object, accepts additional aesthetics. Note specifying layer-specific fill/color requires setting new scale ggnewscale::new_scale_fill/color(); example follows:
code: p <- plotSpatialData(x) # joint all <- p +     plotImage() +     plotLabel(a=1/3) +     plotShape(i = 1) +     plotShape(i = 3) +     new_scale_color() +     plotPoint(col="genes") +     labs(title = "layered") # split one <- list(     p + plotImage() + labs(title = "image"),     p + plotLabel() + labs(title = "labels"),     p + plotShape(i = 1) + labs(title = "circles"),     p + plotShape(i = 3) + labs(title = "polygons"),     p + plotPoint(col="genes") + labs(title = "points")) wrap_plots(c(list(all), one), nrow=2)
